input_api: twisted.names.dns.Message().fromStr(str: bytes) -> None (then the decoded Message fields)
documentation_note: The Twisted API reference documents Message.fromStr: 'Decode a byte string in the format described by RFC 1035 into this Message.'
scope: RFC 1035 message from local bytes: header flags, questions and CNAME/A/AAAA/MX answers with compressed names
family: Twisted Names (twisted/names/dns.py Message.decode, Query, RRHeader, Name and per-type Record_* decoders)
family_note: Own pure-Python decoder in Twisted's DNS package (twisted.names); it uses no other DNS library. Twisted decodes AD and CD but not the reserved Z bit, so z carries AD and CD only (both controls have all three bits clear). A text is Record_A.dottedQuad(); AAAA text is formatted by the harness from the 16 decoded address bytes (RFC 5952). Importing twisted.names.dns imports twisted.internet protocol classes but installs no reactor and opens no socket. Its PyPI count covers the whole Twisted networking framework, not only DNS use.

family_note: Own pure-Python decoder in mitmproxy's DNS flow model; it uses no other DNS library. It keeps the 3-bit field after RA as `reserved`. unpack decompresses names inside CNAME/MX RDATA; the harness reads A/AAAA through the record's ipv4_address/ipv6_address properties, CNAME through domain_name, and the MX preference and exchange from the decompressed RDATA with the library's domain_names.unpack_from. Importing mitmproxy.dns pulls in mitmproxy's flow and connection model (the full runtime requirement set is installed from pinned wheels), but no proxy, server or event loop is started and no socket is opened. Its PyPI count covers the whole interception proxy, not only DNS use.

name: pydns3
license_evidence: Wheel METADATA classifier 'License :: OSI Approved :: MIT License', MIT licence text in the License field and dist-info/LICENSE (sha256 e6b7a7d9...), checked in the image; pystructs3 0.0.8 carries the same MIT LICENSE
input_api: pydns.Message.unpack(raw: bytes, ctx: Optional[pystructs.Context] = None) -> Message (fields id, flags, questions, answers, authority, additional; Answer.content typed A/AAAA/CNAME/MX/NS/PTR/SOA/TXT/SRV)
scope: RFC 1035 message from local bytes: header flags, questions and CNAME/A/AAAA/MX answers with compressed names
family: pydns3 (message.py Message.unpack, answer.py, content.py) over pystructs3 (std.py Domain name codec, struct.py Struct)
family_note: Own pure-Python message codec by Andrew C Scott: pydns declares the header, question, answer and per-type content layouts as pystructs Struct classes, and pystructs3 (the same author's serialization library) unpacks them, including Domain name compression. It uses no other DNS library and is unrelated to the Python 2 PyDNS/py3dns line (it installs the top-level package 'pydns', not 'DNS'). The README's 'Packet Parsing' example documents Message.unpack(raw) on bytes. pydns.Flags keeps AD and CD but not the reserved Z bit, so z carries AD and CD only (both controls have all three bits clear). Message.unpack passes Message itself, not Answer, as the class for non-OPT additional records, so additional records other than OPT would not parse; the controls have none. Only pystructs3, pyderive3 and typing-extensions are installed besides the wheel: pypool3 and pyserve3 are required only by the client and server modules. Found in round 5 through an ecosyste.ms keyword listing (PyPI packages tagged 'dns'), not through the round-3 PyPI name list check. Low adoption (59 downloads in the window).
